Setup Assistant listing copy vs on-device setup engineering — two different jobs

Teams assume Setup Assistant flow documentation covers storefront language. On-device first-run UI and App Store Connect actually separate setup wizard behavior from product-page copy:

  • Setup Assistant on the device — when a user powers on a new or erased iPhone, iPad, or Mac, Setup Assistant walks through language, region, Wi-Fi, Apple ID, restore, Screen Time, and Remote Management enrollment when MDM is assigned. System first-boot behavior — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Remote Management enrollment screens — during Setup Assistant, supervised or MDM-enrolled devices may show Remote Management UI that enrolls the device into an organization's MDM server. Enrollment UX engineering belongs in your app and MDM console — not listing rewrite.
  • Setup Assistant marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app documents Setup Assistant flows, complements Remote Management enrollment, or educates about first-boot setup. Connect text fields — this page.

Setup Assistant vs Apple Configurator, DDM, Return to Service, and Managed Apple ID — hard disambiguation

Apple groups several MDM, prep, and identity features. Indie teams conflate them on one product page. AppLocale covers Setup Assistant on-device first-run UI marketing on listing metadata — not Mac prep tooling, DDM protocol delivery, fleet wipe, or org-account identity as lead:

  • Setup Assistant (this page) — on-device first-boot and out-of-box setup wizard on iPhone, iPad, and Mac: language, Wi-Fi, Apple ID, restore, Screen Time, and Remote Management enrollment screens during initial setup. Gallery frames may show "Setup Assistant" badges, first-boot wizard walkthroughs, Remote Management enrollment UI, or language-and-Wi-Fi setup screens. zh-Hans terms: 设置助理, 初始设置, 开机向导, 开箱设置, 远程管理.
  • Apple Configurator (different) — Mac desktop app for USB-connected device preparation, supervised mode enrollment, blueprints, restore and prepare, and manual fleet prep before MDM — 配置器 vocabulary. See Apple Configurator listing when Mac Configurator USB prep is your lead — not on-device first-run wizard UI. Configurator prepares devices on a Mac — Setup Assistant runs on the device during first boot.
  • Declarative Device Management (different) — MDM configuration protocol that delivers settings, status reports, and software update declarations to already-enrolled managed devices — 声明式设备管理 vocabulary. See Declarative Device Management listing when DDM protocol and configuration declarations are your lead — not Setup Assistant wizard screens. DDM runs on enrolled devices — Setup Assistant is the first-run UI before or during enrollment.
  • Return to Service (different) — MDM admin workflow that erases a supervised or managed device and returns it to a service-ready enrollment state for fleet redeployment — 返回服务 vocabulary. See Return to Service listing when erase-and-return fleet wipe is your lead — not first-boot setup wizard flows. Return to Service is an MDM command issued to enrolled devices — Setup Assistant is the on-device UI during initial configuration.
  • Managed Apple ID (different) — organization accounts issued through Apple School Manager or Apple Business Manager for students and employees — 托管 Apple ID vocabulary. See Managed Apple ID listing when org-account identity is your lead — not Setup Assistant wizard UI. Managed Apple ID is an identity surface — Setup Assistant is the first-run setup experience where users may sign in with org or personal accounts.
  • Automated Device Enrollment / ADE / Account-Driven User Enrollment (enrollment methods — mention only in contrast) — ADE assigns devices to MDM through Apple Business Manager or Apple School Manager before Setup Assistant runs; Account-Driven User Enrollment is a BYOD enrollment method. These are server-side enrollment programs and methods — not the Setup Assistant UI itself. Mention only when your English source genuinely shows both enrollment method and Setup Assistant screens on separate frames.

Your gallery may show a Setup Assistant language screen on one frame and a Remote Management enrollment walkthrough on the next — but listing copy should name each claim accurately per frame. A Setup Assistant badge is not a Configurator blueprint dashboard, not a DDM status report, not a Return to Service erase flow, not a Managed Apple ID sign-in screen, and not an Activation Lock status overlay unless that is what the screenshot shows.

Setup Assistant vs Activation Lock, Find My, and consumer security

MDM and security apps blur several Apple hardening and fleet-management surfaces. AppLocale covers Setup Assistant listing metadata only — link to contrast pages when buyers need disambiguation:

  • Activation Lock (different) — consumer Apple ID activation barrier; device remains locked after erase and cannot be set up without the owner's Apple ID when Find My is on — 激活锁 vocabulary. See Activation Lock listing when post-erase Apple ID gates are your lead — not first-run setup wizard UI.
  • Find My map tracking (different) — item location, AirTag-style find workflows, last-known-location maps — 查找 vocabulary. See Find My listing when location tracking is your lead — not Setup Assistant first-boot flows.
  • Lost Mode locate and play sound (different) — lock a lost device remotely, display a message, play a sound, and track location on a map — 丢失模式 vocabulary folded into Find My marketing. Lost Mode helps locate a missing device — it is not Setup Assistant language-and-Wi-Fi setup screens.
  • Stolen Device Protection (different) — optional theft hardening under Settings → Face ID & Passcode → Stolen Device Protection; requires Face ID or Touch ID for sensitive actions away from familiar locations and adds Security Delay — 失窃设备保护 vocabulary. See Stolen Device Protection listing when passcode-delay hardening is your lead — not Setup Assistant marketing.
  • Lockdown Mode (different) — optional extreme protection against sophisticated cyberattacks under Settings → Privacy & Security → Lockdown Mode — 锁定模式 vocabulary. See Lockdown Mode listing — not Setup Assistant.

If your US page leads with Setup Assistant, zh-Hans copy should stay on 设置助理 and 初始设置 — not drift into Activation Lock 激活锁 language, Find My map tracking, Configurator 配置器 Mac prep badges, DDM 声明式设备管理 protocol jargon, Return to Service 返回服务 wipe flows, Managed Apple ID 托管 Apple ID sign-in pitches, Stolen Device Protection Security Delay marketing, or Lockdown Mode extreme-protection claims unless those are genuinely separate gallery frames with accurate English source claims.

What Apple Setup Assistant actually does — listing honesty

Apple ships Setup Assistant as the on-device first-boot and out-of-box setup wizard on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. When a user powers on a new or erased device, Setup Assistant walks through language and region, Wi-Fi connection, Apple ID sign-in or skip, restore from iCloud or computer backup, Screen Time, and Remote Management enrollment when the device is assigned to an organization's MDM. Third-party MDM, device-management, and education apps may complement this by documenting Setup Assistant flows, surfacing Remote Management enrollment guidance, or educating fleet admins about first-run setup. Setup Assistant–specific vocabulary — what translates differently in zh-Hans

First-boot and out-of-box setup marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general localization guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate Setup Assistant — not a literal paste of US marketing:

设置助理 (Setup Assistant)

Apple's Chinese MDM, education, and enterprise support materials use 设置助理 for the on-device first-boot and out-of-box setup wizard on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Enterprise marketing may also keep Setup Assistant on technical frames when accurate to your English source. AppLocale picks the term buyers recognize on each screenshot — a first-run walkthrough frame needs 设置助理-friendly phrasing; a technical badge may keep Setup Assistant when that matches your gallery.

初始设置 (initial setup)

US pages use "Initial setup" or "First-boot setup" for the sequence of screens users complete when powering on a new device. China storefront copy often uses 初始设置 or 新机设置 when describing Setup Assistant-centric flows — distinct from Configurator 恢复与准备 (restore and prepare) bench workflows or Return to Service 返回服务 MDM erase commands.

开机向导 (first-boot wizard)

Marketing frames that show the step-by-step first-power-on experience use 开机向导 when your English source genuinely markets wizard-style walkthroughs through language, Wi-Fi, and Apple ID — not generic "easy setup" overclaims your screenshots do not support.

开箱设置 (out-of-box setup)

Enterprise and education buyers describe unboxing a fleet device and running through Setup Assistant as 开箱设置 — the out-of-box experience before the device reaches daily use. zh-Hans copy uses 开箱设置 on workflow frames that show OOBE sequences — separate from Mac Configurator 设备准备 (device preparation) at a prep bench.

远程管理 (Remote Management)

During Setup Assistant on supervised or MDM-assigned devices, users may see Remote Management screens that enroll the device into an organization's MDM server. zh-Hans marketing uses 远程管理 on enrollment frames — not as a promise that your app issues Return to Service wipes or configures ADE portals.

AppLocale FAQ

What is Apple Setup Assistant and why does listing copy matter?

Setup Assistant is the on-device first-boot and out-of-box setup wizard on iPhone, iPad, and Mac — language, Wi-Fi, Apple ID, restore, and Remote Management enrollment screens during initial configuration. Marketing that wizard UI on your en-US page does not auto-fill zh-Hans Connect fields.

Does Setup Assistant documentation auto-translate my China listing?

No. Setup Assistant is on-device first-run UI — it does not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback on the product page.

What listing fields does AppLocale rewrite for Setup Assistant apps?

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) copy for App Store Connect listing fields you specify: title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines that mention Setup Assistant, first-boot setup, Remote Management screens, or out-of-box wizard flows — rewritten from your English originals with terms like 设置助理, 初始设置, and 开箱设置 where accurate.

How is this different from Apple Configurator, DDM, Return to Service, or Managed Apple ID?

Setup Assistant listing copy markets on-device first-boot and out-of-box setup wizard UI. Configurator listing copy markets Mac desktop device preparation and supervision enrollment. DDM listing copy markets the MDM configuration protocol for settings and status reports. Return to Service listing copy markets the MDM admin erase-and-return workflow. Managed Apple ID listing copy markets org-account identity through ASM/ABM. Listing vocabulary must follow your English lead feature.

How is this different from ADE, Activation Lock, Find My, Stolen Device Protection, or Lockdown Mode?

Setup Assistant is the on-device first-run setup wizard. ADE and Account-Driven User Enrollment are server-side enrollment methods — mention only in contrast. Activation Lock prevents consumer reactivation without the owner's Apple ID after erase. Find My and Lost Mode help locate missing devices. Stolen Device Protection adds biometric gates and Security Delay. Lockdown Mode is extreme cyberattack hardening. Each is a separate Apple feature — do not reuse boilerplate across them.

Does AppLocale implement Setup Assistant flows or bypass Activation Lock?

No. We deliver listing metadata copy only. MDM engineering, Configurator blueprint configuration, ADE portal setup, and Activation Lock bypass are outside AppLocale scope. We rewrite how you describe existing Setup Assistant workflows on the store page — we do not control first-boot UI at runtime.

What character limits apply to zh-Hans Setup Assistant fields?

App name and subtitle are each up to 30 characters. Keywords allow up to 100 characters. Description and screenshot caption lines have longer limits but should stay concise — especially overlays that must fit on-device mockups.
